title: The Extraterrestrial Rings of Bronze Age Greece
gist: A new archaeological study used portable X-ray fluorescence to test 91 Bronze Age Greek artifacts for meteorite-derived iron, showing that humans crafted iron jewelry and tools from space rocks long before smelting technology existed.

themes.theme: Meteoritic iron before the Iron Age

insights.claim: Long before humans developed smelting technology to extract iron from ore, they worked iron sourced from meteorites into tools and jewelry.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Shows that metallurgical value was recognized from extraterrestrial material millennia before humans could produce iron themselves.
insights.quote: Long before humans developed the smelting technology to extract iron from ore, they were using the metal to make tools, jewelry, and more.

insights.claim: King Tut's dagger was crafted from meteorite iron well before the Iron Age began.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A famous artifact serves as concrete proof that pre-Iron-Age elites already valued worked meteoritic metal.
insights.quote: King Tut’s dagger, for example, was crafted from meteorite iron well before the Iron Age.

insights.claim: A new study published in the Journal of Archaeological Science uncovered meteorite jewelry trends from Bronze Age Greece.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Extends the known geography and chronology of meteoritic-iron use into Bronze Age Greek material culture.
insights.quote: Now, a new study published in the Journal of Archaeological Science has uncovered meteorite jewelry trends from Bronze Age Greece.

insights.claim: Meteoritic iron can be distinguished from smelted iron by its unusually high nickel content, detectable with portable X-ray fluorescence machines resembling price-scanning guns.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Gives archaeologists a fast, non-destructive field method to sort space-derived artifacts from earthly ones.
insights.quote: Iron from space contains high amounts of the element and portable X-ray fluorescence machines, which look like price-scanning guns, can detect the concentrations in a snap.
insights.locator: How can you tell if iron comes from a meteorite

insights.claim: A team of archaeologists tested 91 artifacts excavated from 33 different sites to determine whether they were made from meteorite iron.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Establishes the scale of the survey underlying the study's jewelry-trend conclusions.
insights.quote: So a team of archaeologists zapped 91 artifacts excavated from 33 different sites to find out if they were truly out of this world.
insights.locator: How can you tell if iron comes from a meteorite
